question.worked_solution:
Let $u=1+{tan}^{3}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{tan}^{2}⁡x\cdot {sec}^{2}⁡x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u={tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x}{1+{tan}^{3}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{1+{tan}^{3}⁡x}\cdot {tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot (\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|1+{tan}^{3}⁡x|+C \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡|1+{tan}^{3}⁡x|}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$
